## Selective read-only support during implementation

Planning and implementation now explicitly consider useful independent reader assignments while
keeping one writer and a ceiling of two readers. Each assignment must replace necessary work or
address a concrete risk of rework. Distinct questions, bounded evidence, concise handoffs, and
planned batch review keep parallelism from becoming continuous supervision.

The optional `harness-agent` runner adds `--writer` for a single writer working alongside
`--shared` readers. Default exclusive access retains isolation. Another writer still waits, and
overlapping nested writer/reader jobs are rejected before queueing. Existing job records remain
compatible; older runners conservatively treat the new writer mode as exclusive.

Readers must not alter source, Git state, or shared build/test outputs. Access flags are assignment
and coordination contracts, not filesystem sandboxes. Findings on unfinished work remain
provisional; one independent approval review consumes the completed batch and existing proof.

No scheduler, model defaults, collector, or per-step reporting is added. The initial goal of less
than 25% median token premium is a calibration target, not a measured saving or runtime cutoff.
This release retains the 2.5.0 startup integration and compatible automatic-update source range.
